name: Vachr Appointments – Free Appointment Booking with PayPal & Stripe
author: vachr

sections.description:
Turn your WordPress site into a 24/7 booking desk for doctors, private practices, hairdressers, barbers, massage therapists, beauty and wellness providers, and other appointment-based businesses. Clients choose a service, provider and available time online, while you manage schedules, reservations and customer records in one place.

Whether you work on your own or run a small team, Vachr Appointments helps cut down on booking calls and message exchanges. Set each provider’s availability, let clients book from your site, accept online or offline payments, and use the waiting list to offer newly freed appointments to interested customers.

Everything is free

Many booking plugins give you a basic free version and put staff, online payments or reminders behind a paid upgrade. Vachr Appointments has no Pro version, no add-ons to buy and no license key:

  • No limits on providers, services or bookings.
  • No commission and no monthly fee. Online payments go straight to your own PayPal, Stripe or Mollie account; bank transfers and cash cost nothing.
  • No external booking service and no sign-up. Bookings and customer records stay in your WordPress database.

Why salons, practices and therapists choose it

  • Fewer empty slots after cancellations: the waiting list offers the freed time to other customers automatically.
  • Running late? Set the delay on the reception desk and the customers who are coming are told the expected start by email, on their reservation page and on a waiting-room screen.
  • A reception desk for staff without WordPress accounts: a password-protected page with the day, week and month calendar and one-click walk-in booking.
  • Bookings in your own calendar: every provider gets a private calendar feed for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook, and customers get an “Add to Google Calendar” link in their confirmation email.
  • Chair rental and shared practices: every provider can have their own bank account and PayPal, Stripe or Mollie account, so each one is paid directly.
  • Connect other systems: webhooks call an SMS gateway, CRM or Zapier when a reservation is created, paid, changed or cancelled – with your own URL, headers and body.
  • Get paid by bank transfer without checking statements: QR payment codes and automatic matching of bank notification emails to reservations.
  • Receipts and proforma invoices with your numbering, tax details and document language.
  • Ready for European businesses: 13 translations, multiple currencies, consent handling and Czech, Slovak, Swiss and SEPA payment QR codes.

External services

This plugin connects to external services only when the site owner enables and configures the related feature.

  • Stripe: When a customer chooses Stripe for an online payment, the site sends Stripe the reservation description and ID, amount, currency, customer email address, and return URLs to create a hosted checkout session. The plugin also asks Stripe for the payment status when processing its webhook. Stripe’s Services Agreement and Privacy Policy apply.
  • PayPal: When a customer chooses PayPal, the site sends PayPal the reservation description and ID, amount, currency, the site name and return and cancel URLs to create an order, and captures that order when the customer returns. The site obtains an access token from PayPal with the client ID and secret configured by the site owner. PayPal’s User Agreement and Privacy Statement apply.
  • Mollie: When a customer chooses Mollie, the site sends Mollie the reservation description and ID, amount, currency, and redirect and webhook URLs to create a payment. The plugin retrieves that payment’s status from Mollie when processing its webhook. Mollie’s User Agreement and Privacy Statement apply.
  • Google Calendar and other calendar apps: The plugin does not connect to Google itself. If a provider subscribes to their private calendar feed in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook or another calendar app, that service downloads the feed from your site; it contains the provider’s reservations with the service, time and the customer’s name, phone and email. The “Add to Google Calendar” link in the confirmation email opens Google Calendar with the service, provider name, time and reservation number when the customer clicks it. Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy apply to Google Calendar.
  • Webhooks: If the site owner adds a webhook (Appointments -> Settings -> Webhooks), the site sends an HTTP request to the URL the owner entered whenever a selected event happens. The request contains what the owner put in the URL, headers and body, which can include the reservation number, service, time, price and the customer’s name, email and phone. Nothing is sent unless a webhook is configured and active. The privacy policy of the receiving service applies.
  • IMAP mailbox: If the site owner enables email payment import, the site connects to the IMAP server configured by the owner to read bank notification messages and match them to reservations. Mailbox credentials and message contents are sent only to that configured mail server; parsed message contents are not stored by the plugin.

Booking

  • Public booking form via the [vachr_appointment_form] shortcode, a block or an Elementor widget. The reception desk is available as an Elementor widget too.
  • Each provider has their own working hours, calendar rules, photo, link and phone number.
  • Services with their own duration and price; optional overtime surcharge per started 30-minute block.
  • Restrict the form to a provider or service and override language or currency with shortcode attributes.
  • Hovering a provider icon on the time slots shows a card with an enlarged photo and full name.
  • Reception desk [vachr_appointment_desk]: day, week and month calendar with a date picker, reservations, one-click walk-in booking, deleting unpaid and cancelling paid reservations, usable behind a password-protected page. Staff can also cancel a day or a range of days (for example when the provider is ill) and notify the customers.
  • Calendar feed per provider: subscribe to a private address in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook to see pending and confirmed reservations there; the address can be replaced at any time. Confirmation emails include an “Add to Google Calendar” link.
  • Delays: when a provider runs late, the booking form warns visitors, the customer’s reservation page shows the expected later start, and the waiting room shortcode [vachr_appointment_status provider="1"] shows the delay and the expected start of the remaining times of the day (no personal data, refreshes itself).

Payments

  • PayPal, Stripe and Mollie online payments (Stripe and Mollie checkout shows the methods enabled in your account, such as cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay or iDEAL), verified with the gateway before a reservation is marked paid.
  • Bank transfer with a bank account per currency and payment instructions in every content language; QR payment codes for Czech (SPAYD), Slovak (PAY by square), Swiss (QR-bill) and other SEPA (EPC) accounts.
  • Own payment details for every provider, for example a salon where providers rent a chair: separate bank accounts (QR codes and payment instructions follow the provider) and separate PayPal, Stripe or Mollie keys, so each provider is paid directly. Providers without their own details use the site-wide ones.
  • Cash payments.
  • Email payment import: match bank notification emails from an IMAP inbox to reservations by number, amount and currency, with a parser profile per bank.

Customers and reservations

  • Customer records linked to reservations by email, with a searchable directory and contact cards.
  • Upcoming reservations separated from appointment history; notes, contact windows and archiving.
  • Optional country, street, phone and language fields, each of which can be made required.
  • Typed custom fields with translated labels, descriptions and dropdown choices, assignable to each service.

Waiting list

  • Customers can wait for taken times or for any time.
  • When a time is freed they receive an email with a confirmation link; the first to confirm gets it.
  • Notify one after another or all at once, with configurable confirmation time and entry lifetime.

Invoicing and email

  • Printable receipts and proforma invoices with configurable numbering, supplier and tax details and document language.
  • Reservation emails and receipts show the final price including surcharges.

Multilingual and multi-currency

  • Translations: Czech, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Slovak and Ukrainian. English is the source language.
  • Multiple currencies with a base currency and configurable content languages.

Design and protection

  • Appearance settings for accent and surface colors, corner radius and maximum width.
  • Built-in CAPTCHA and consent handling on the public form.
  • Data is stored in the plugin’s own vachr_appointment_* tables.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/vachr-appointments or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate Vachr Appointments. Activation creates the plugin’s tables.
  3. Open Appointments → Settings to set currencies, languages and payment methods.
  4. Create providers, working hours and services under the Appointments menu.
  5. Add [vachr_appointment_form] to a page.
sections.faq:
Is it really free? Is there a Pro version?

Yes, it is free. There is no Pro version, no paid add-on and no limit on providers, services or bookings. All features described here are included. You only pay the usual fees of PayPal, Stripe or Mollie if you use them.

How do I show the booking form?

Add the shortcode [vachr_appointment_form] to a page. To restrict it, use for example [vachr_appointment_form provider="1" service="2" language="cs" currency="CZK"].

The Vachr Appointments block supports selecting multiple services and providers. Choose All to remove a restriction. Shortcodes also accept comma-separated IDs, for example [vachr_appointment_form provider="1,3" service="2,4"].

Can staff book for customers?

Yes. Use the reception desk [vachr_appointment_desk] described below.

How do I set up the reception desk for walk-in customers?

  1. Create a page and add [vachr_appointment_desk provider="1"] (use the provider’s ID; leave provider out to show all providers).
  2. In the page settings set Visibility to Password protected and choose a password.
  3. Staff open the page, enter the password and see today’s reservations with all details (service, customer, phone, note). Switch between Day, Week and Month, or pick any date. Clicking a free time books it; name, phone and note are optional and no email is sent. Open a reservation to delete it (unpaid) or cancel it (paid).

No WordPress login is needed. Create one page and password per provider if every provider should see only their own calendar. Administrators and Appointment staff can use the page while logged in, even without a password.

Does it work with Google Calendar?

Yes, in one direction. Every provider has a private calendar feed (provider settings -> Calendar rules). Add it in Google Calendar under Other calendars -> From URL, or subscribe to it in Apple Calendar or Outlook, and the provider’s reservations appear there. No Google account connection or Google Cloud project is needed. Google refreshes subscribed calendars only every several hours, so use the reception desk for the live schedule. Events in Google Calendar do not block times in the booking form yet.

How do customers in the waiting room see a delay?

Add [vachr_appointment_status provider="1"] to a page (it also works on a password-protected page). It shows whether the provider is on time or how many minutes late, and the booked and expected start of the remaining times of today. Attributes: upcoming="0" hides the table, refresh="60" sets the automatic refresh in seconds (0 = off), language="cs" sets the language. The delay itself is set on the reception desk.

Can customers see their reservation online?

Yes. The confirmation email links to a private reservation page with the appointment details, payment status, bank transfer instructions with a QR code, online payment and the proforma invoice or receipt. Unpaid reservations can switch between the payment methods the provider offers. If you enable cancellation, customers can also cancel there, with fee levels depending on how long before the appointment they cancel.

Can the plugin call other systems, for example an SMS gateway?

Yes. Under Appointments -> Settings -> Webhooks you can add webhooks that are sent when a reservation is created, confirmed, paid, cancelled, changed or declined, or when a delay is announced. Set the URL, the method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE), headers and body, and insert variables such as {customer_phone}, {service_name}, {date} or {start_time}. Requests are sent in the background and retried twice on failure; the last calls are listed on the same page, and every webhook has a test button.

Which payment methods are supported?

PayPal, Stripe, Mollie, bank transfer with QR codes, cash and automatic matching of bank notification emails.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • New: Webhooks (Appointments -> Settings -> Webhooks). Call another system, for example an SMS gateway, a CRM or Zapier, when a reservation is created, confirmed, paid, cancelled, declined by the provider or changed, or when a provider delay is announced.
  • Set the URL, the method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), headers and body for each webhook. Variables such as {customer_phone}, {service_name}, {date}, {start_time}, {booking_id} and the custom fields can be used everywhere and are escaped for the place they are used.
  • Requests are sent in the background so they never slow down a booking; a failed request is retried twice. A log of the recent calls and a test button are on the settings tab, together with a short quick-start guide.
  • All 13 translations updated.
  • No database changes.

1.2.2

  • New: when editing a reservation at the reception desk you can tick “Enter the exact time manually” and type any time down to the minute instead of choosing one of the free slots. The time must not overlap another reservation.
  • The delay email to customers now contains a link to their reservation page.
  • Fix: setting a delay now reports an error when it could not be saved, instead of silently showing it as saved.
  • No database changes.

1.2.1

  • New: calendar feed for every provider. Subscribe to the private address (provider settings -> Calendar rules) in Google Calendar (Other calendars -> From URL), Apple Calendar or Outlook to see the provider’s pending and confirmed reservations there. No Google account connection or Google Cloud project is needed. Google refreshes subscribed calendars only every several hours.
  • The feed address contains a secret token. “Create a new address” replaces it and the old address stops working.
  • The customer’s confirmation email contains an “Add to Google Calendar” link.
  • Preparation for importing events of an external calendar: they can block a provider’s time through a new table. The import itself is not available yet.
  • The database schema is updated (a new column of the providers table and a new table).

1.2.0

  • New: PayPal online payments (Orders API v2) next to Stripe and Mollie. Enter the client ID and secret under Bookings -> Settings -> Payments; a sandbox mode is available for testing.
  • Providers can use their own PayPal account under “Own card payments”, so the money goes directly to them.
  • The reservation is confirmed when the customer returns from PayPal and the payment is captured.

1.1.5

  • Reception desk: find an existing customer by name, email or phone while booking, or enter an email (optional) and choose whether a confirmation email is sent to the customer.
  • Delay notice on the customer’s reservation page: if a provider is running late today and the reservation is pushed back, the page shows the expected later start.
  • Delay notice in the booking form: when a provider has a delay today, visitors see a warning above the calendar.
  • New waiting room shortcode [vachr_appointment_status provider="1"] showing today’s delay and the expected start of the remaining times, without personal data. It refreshes itself (refresh seconds, upcoming="0" hides the table, language sets the language).
  • Reception desk: the date shown as “today” follows the current view, and a restore page link and form action were corrected.
  • New translations of the new texts in every bundled language.

1.1.4

  • Reception desk: new “Cancel day” button. It cancels all open reservations of a provider for today (default) or a range of days, for example when the provider falls ill. An optional explanation is added to the email that is sent to the customers by default (each in their own language). Paid reservations are cancelled too and are not refunded automatically.
  • Cancelling a day also closes the calendar for those days, so nothing can be booked and the waiting list sends no offers while the days are closed.
  • The closed days are listed in the same dialog and can be reopened there, without going to the administration.
  • When reopening, customers can be asked to confirm their cancelled reservation (on by default, 24 hours by default). The time is held for them and they get an email with a confirmation link. Reservations not confirmed in time are cancelled for good and the freed times go to the waiting list. Without this option the reservations are cancelled for good immediately.
  • New reservation status “Awaiting customer confirmation”, shown on the reception desk, in the reservations admin and on the customer’s reservation page.
  • New translations of all new texts in every bundled language.
  • The database schema is updated (two new columns of the reservations table).

1.1.3

  • The reception desk has a Day (default, reservations listed one under another), Week and Month view and a date picker to jump to any date.
  • The reception desk can delete unpaid reservations and cancel paid ones (a cancelled paid reservation is not refunded automatically).
  • Provider delay on the reception desk: enter the delay in minutes (or use a quick button), and the next minutes of the calendar are blocked for new bookings. Customers whose reservation is really pushed back (until a free gap absorbs the delay) can be notified by email; choose how many of them (all by default) or only adjust the calendar without sending email.
  • Removed the [vachr_appointment_staff] shortcode, block and widget: the reception desk does the same job. Use [vachr_appointment_desk] instead.

1.1.2

  • New reception desk shortcode [vachr_appointment_desk]: a week calendar of a provider with all reservations (service, customer, phone, note) and one-click walk-in booking without a name or email. Works behind a password-protected page, so staff need no WordPress login. A provider sees only the calendar named in the shortcode.
  • The reception desk is also available as a Gutenberg block, and the booking form and reception desk as Elementor widgets.

1.1.1

  • Fixed saving a provider after using “Bulk change” for overtime with a date in the past (or with older overtime values): the browser silently blocked the form and nothing was saved.
  • Overtime hour fields now accept any value between 0 and 12 hours.

1.1.0

  • Every provider can have their own bank accounts and their own Stripe or Mollie keys (provider page, Payment step). Bank transfer instructions, QR codes, e-mails, receipts and online payments then use the details of the provider of the reservation. Providers without their own details keep using the site-wide settings.
  • Stripe webhooks of a provider with their own keys use a provider-specific URL shown on the provider page, and can only confirm that provider’s reservations.
  • Translations of the new settings in all bundled languages. The database gets two new columns on update.

1.0.18

  • Fixed the reservation page labels for the provider and date and time.
  • Updated the affected translations in all bundled languages.

1.0.17

  • Customers can cancel a reservation themselves from their reservation page. Switch it on in Settings > Cancellation.
  • Configurable fee levels: for example free cancellation at least 48 hours before the appointment, a 50 % fee at least 24 hours before, and either no online cancellation or a fixed fee for shorter notice. Fees are a percentage of the reservation total.
  • The customer sees the fee levels and what cancelling costs right now, and confirms before the reservation is cancelled. The time is freed for the waiting list.
  • The customer, the site owner and the provider get an email with the amount to refund or to collect. Refunds and fees are not moved automatically. The reservations list shows the fee and refund.
  • A payment that arrives after the customer cancelled keeps the reservation cancelled and notifies the site owner.
  • Free reservations now also get the link to the reservation page when cancellation is enabled.
  • Translations of all new texts into all bundled languages.

1.0.16

  • Translations of the new appearance settings and preview into all bundled languages.

1.0.15

  • Appearance settings: choose from eight ready-made themes (including two dark ones) and three designs, and fine-tune colors for the form, calendar days and available or occupied times, text, background, corner radius, width and font size.
  • Live preview of the booking form (calendar, times, fields, summary) with a desktop and mobile view, updated as you change the settings.

1.0.14

  • Reservations that need the provider’s approval (overtime or provider confirmation enabled) now send the customer an email right away, saying the reservation awaits confirmation or decline, with a link to the reservation page. The customer is emailed again once the provider decides.
  • New customer reservation page: the confirmation email links to a private page with the appointment, status, price, payment (bank transfer with QR code, online payment or cash, changeable while unpaid) and the proforma invoice or receipt.
  • Custom fields can be assigned to each service: tick the fields to show in the booking form of that service. Existing services keep showing all fields until saved.
  • Bank transfers: add a bank account per currency (IBAN, BIC, account holder). An account without a currency is the default for currencies without their own account, and a bank transfer is offered only for currencies that have an account.
  • Bank transfer instructions can be written separately for every content language, with placeholders such as {holder}, {iban}, {amount} and {reference}. When left empty they are generated from the account and translated.
  • QR payment codes follow the country of the IBAN and the currency: Czech QR payment, Slovak PAY by square, Swiss QR-bill and EPC QR for other SEPA accounts. IBANs with an invalid check digit are reported and get no QR code.
  • Email payment import: one parser profile per bank, selected by the sender address or domain, each with its own reference, amount and currency patterns. The previous single setting is converted to a profile automatically.
  • Fixed the payment QR code not being drawn on the public pages and the receipt.
  • Fixed saving one settings tab clearing the options of the other tabs (for example payment gateway keys and invoicing details).
  • Fixed email translations falling back to the site language after a nested language switch.

1.0.13

  • Each working-hours row can have an optional break (e.g. lunch); no reservation can overlap it.

1.0.11

  • The Vachr Appointments block supports multiple services and providers, including filtered availability and waiting lists. Existing single selections remain supported; shortcodes accept comma-separated IDs.
  • Providers can choose how paid overtime is booked: standard booking, filling from the earliest time with a configurable maximum gap, or charging for each unfilled started 30-minute overtime block before the appointment.

1.0.10

  • Removed the unused license-key activation system. Appointment booking features no longer ask for a license key or contact a license server.
  • Updated the plugin introduction to speak directly to doctors, salons, independent professionals and small service teams.

1.0.9

  • Provider edit page: Save and Archive toolbar, step buttons and cleaner field layout with photo preview.
  • Providers have a new optional phone number.

1.0.8

  • Hover card with enlarged photo and full name for providers on time slots.
  • Providers have a new optional link.

1.0.7

  • Searchable country calling code, country and language fields.
  • Phone, street, country and language can each be required.

1.0.6

  • Customers can store a country, street and language; the booking form can ask for them.

1.0.5

  • Waiting list for services, with its own settings and admin page.

1.0.4

  • Customer records, directory, contact cards, notes, custom fields and reservation history.

1.0.3

  • Optional overtime surcharge per currency and per started 30-minute block.

short_description: Free appointment booking, no Pro version: unlimited providers, PayPal, Stripe & Mollie, bank QR payments, waiting list, invoices, reception desk.

upgrade_notice.1.3.0: New: webhooks that call other systems (SMS gateway, CRM, Zapier) when a reservation changes. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.1.2.2: New: exact manual time when editing a reservation at the reception desk, and a link to the reservation page in delay emails. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: New: PayPal as an online payment gateway next to Stripe and Mollie. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.1.1.5: New: delay notices on the booking form and the customer's reservation page, a waiting room shortcode [vachr_appointment_status], and customer search on the reception desk. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.1.1.4: New: cancel a day or a range of days on the reception desk (for example when the provider is ill), with an email to the customers, and reopen the days with the option to let customers confirm their cancelled reservation. The database gets two new columns on update.
upgrade_notice.1.1.3: New: day, week and month view and delay notifications on the reception desk; delete or cancel reservations there. The staff booking shortcode [vachr_appointment_staff] was removed: use [vachr_appointment_desk]. The database gets a new table on update.
upgrade_notice.1.1.2: New: reception desk calendar with quick walk-in booking, usable behind a password-protected page. Nothing changes until you add the shortcode.
upgrade_notice.1.1.1: Fixes a provider that could not be saved after a bulk overtime change with a past date.
upgrade_notice.1.0.19: New: separate bank accounts and Stripe or Mollie keys for each provider, e.g. for salons with providers renting space. Nothing changes until you fill them in. The database gets two new columns on update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.18: Fixed reservation page labels and updated their translations.
upgrade_notice.1.0.17: New: customers can cancel their reservation from the reservation page, with configurable fee levels (off by default, Settings > Cancellation). The database gets two new columns on update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.16: The new appearance themes and live preview are now translated.
upgrade_notice.1.0.15: Booking form appearance: ready-made themes, more color options and a live preview in the settings.
upgrade_notice.1.0.14: Custom fields per service, bank accounts per currency, translated transfer instructions, QR codes for CZ, SK, CH and SEPA accounts, bank-specific email parser profiles and a fix for settings being cleared when saving another tab.
upgrade_notice.1.0.10: Appointments no longer require or check a license key. The refreshed description explains who the plugin is for.
upgrade_notice.1.0.9: Provider edit page improvements and an optional provider phone number.
